name: Calendar Straddle (Straddle Swap)
summary: Sell the front-month straddle and buy the back-month straddle at the same strike; a double-weighted single-strike calendar that maximizes theta and vega at one price point.

legs.strike_rule: ATM strike, |delta| 0.45-0.55; the same strike is used for all four legs.

max_profit: Roughly double a single ATM calendar: the back-month straddle's value at front expiry with spot at the strike, minus the debit. Typically 20-40% of the debit but with twice the dollar sensitivity.
max_loss: The net debit paid, if spot ends far from the strike at front expiry.
breakevens: Two, bracketing the strike, marginally wider than a single calendar because the debit is larger: approximately strike +/- (1.0 to 1.2) x (debit/2) x 2 in underlying points. Solve numerically.

greeks.delta: ~0 at the ATM strike and stays flatter than a single calendar because the call and put calendar deltas offset as spot drifts
greeks.vega: positive, roughly 2x a single calendar - the most vega-dense structure in the family per dollar of debit

when_to_use: IV rank < 25 with a strong pin thesis at a specific strike (max-pain level, heavy OI strike, a long-standing consolidation midpoint). The advantage over a plain calendar is that put-call skew asymmetries are neutralized and the delta stays flatter through drift; the disadvantage is double the vega.
entry_rules: front_IV - back_IV >= -2.0 vol points on BOTH the call and the put.
Single ATM strike, |delta| 0.45-0.55, chosen at the highest-open-interest strike within 1 ATR of spot when a pin thesis exists.
Total debit <= 3% of equity; combined 4-leg bid-ask <= 8% of debit.
No earnings or ex-dividend inside the front cycle.

LEVEL 3 OK: the short front call is covered by the long back call at the same strike, and the short front put by the long back put. Submit as a single 4-leg mleg; if rejected, submit two 2-leg calendars (call calendar and put calendar), LONG leg first on each.
management_rules: If |spot - strike| > 0.8 x front-month ATM straddle price, close - the pin thesis has failed.
If |net delta| > 0.35 per unit, close rather than adjust; recentering a calendar straddle costs four legs of slippage.
Roll both shorts out one expiry at front DTE <= 7 only if both shorts' |delta| <= 0.60, for a net credit.
exit_rules: Close or roll BOTH short legs by 14:30 ET on front expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the whole structure no later than 2 trading days before front expiry if not rolling.

Whichever short goes ITM: close it immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05 or |delta| >= 0.90. Note that at expiry one of the two shorts is ALWAYS ITM by definition unless spot lands exactly on the strike - this structure guarantees an assignment candidate.
Close the short call before ex-dividend if extrinsic < dividend per share.
assignment_risk: Structurally the highest routine risk of the level-3 calendars, because at front expiry one of the two short legs is essentially always ITM (spot is rarely exactly at the strike). Both shorts are covered by same-strike back-month longs, so the exposure is a covered stock position, but the forced close is not optional here - it is the core of the trade plan.
buying_power: Net debit only; both shorts are strike-for-strike covered.
liquidity_needs: Four legs at one strike, so only the strike's liquidity matters: OI >= 500 in both expiries, quoted spread <= $0.10 per leg. SPY/QQQ/IWM and mega-cap single names.
common_mistakes: Loading double vega in a falling-IV tape; assuming the delta stays neutral (it does not once spot leaves the strike - the ITM side dominates); forgetting that one short leg is always in the money at expiry; adjusting instead of closing.
zero_dte_notes: Not recommended: a 0DTE short straddle against 1-4 DTE longs guarantees one ITM short at the bell on a share-settled name.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
